summary:
I found specs for 52 parts across compute, carriers, cameras, LiDAR/ToF, IMU, batteries, DC-DC, safety/power, CAN and microphones. Every number has its URL in the sources field, accessed 2026-11-07. Values I calculated (Wh, C-rating amps, W) are marked as my calculations in the notes. Fields with no figure in any source I could read are null and explained in the notes. Labels: 29 sourced, 23 partially_sourced, none fully unverified.

Main results:

1. Incumbent battery confirmed. The Gens ace G-Tech 3300 mAh 6S 60C EC5 is 138 x 42 x 43 mm and 506 g on both genstattu.com and BuddyRC (USD 107.19). By my calculation it holds 73.3 Wh, enough for about 220 W average over 20 min, or about 176 W using 80% of capacity.

2. Batteries:
- 6S 5000 mAh LiPo: 755 g.
- Tattu Plus 6S 10000 mAh: 1517 g.
- Gens ace 12S 5000 mAh: 1542 g and 324 mm long.
- Two 3300 packs in series (12S): 1012 g, 146.5 Wh (my calculation).
- 21700 Li-ion packs reach about 220-230 Wh/kg against about 145 for LiPo, but with much lower continuous current:
  - Flywoo 6S1P P45B: 433.7 g, 45 A.
  - Flywoo 6S2P P45B: 860.7 g.
  - Lumenier NAV 6S 5000 mAh: 499 g, 20-35 A.
  - Dan-Tech 6S3P-50S: 1.4 kg, 324 Wh, 75 A, with an optional BMS that reports over CAN.
- Molicel P45B cell (21.4 x 70 mm, 70 g max, 45 A) is included for custom packs.
- Tool packs: Makita BL1860B (18 V 6 Ah, 0.66 kg, retailer data) and Milwaukee M18 FORGE XC8.0 (2.45 lb). Neither maker publishes a continuous current rating.

3. Compute:
- Orin Nano Super devkit: 103 x 90.5 x 34.77 mm per NVIDIA's datasheet, but NVIDIA's family page says 100 x 79 x 21 mm. Mass 174 g comes from an NVIDIA forum post. Modes 7/15/25 W plus MAXN SUPER. Ships with a 19 V supply. USD 399 at SparkFun (launch price USD 249).
- Orin NX 16GB: 69.6 x 45 mm SO-DIMM, 157 TOPS in Super mode, 10/15/25/40 W plus MAXN SUPER. Now USD 1099 at Seeed.
- AGX Orin 64GB devkit: 110 x 110 x 71.65 mm, 872.5 g (forum), 15-60 W, USD 3499. I could not confirm a current 32GB devkit SKU.
- Jetson Orin Nano 2 (78 TOPS, same form factor) is announced for H1 2027 and cannot be bought yet.

4. Carriers:
- Only the Connect Tech Hadron-DM (82.6 x 58.8 mm, 56 g, 9-60 V input, USD 410) can run directly from a 6S or 12S bus. It has no CAN port.
- Seeed J401 (100 x 80 mm, 9-19 V, USD 111): its CAN header is TTL level, so it needs an external transceiver.
- Seeed A603 (87 x 52 x 26 mm, 50 g, 9-20 V, CAN with transceiver, USD 199).
- Seeed Super J401 (71 x 136 x 8.5 mm, 155.8 g, 12-19 V, USD 159).
- Auvidea JNX42 (80 x 104.6 mm, CAN with TJA1051 transceiver, 12 V or 12-48 V with an add-on).
- All of these except the Hadron-DM need a regulated input when fed from 6S (25.2 V full).

5. Regulators on a 12S bus (50.4 V full): the Pololu D36V50F12 (50 V max) and D24V10F5 (36 V max) cannot be used. The D42V110F12 (12-60 V in, 12 V at 9 A, 15 g, USD 69.95) and Mean Well DDR-120C (33.6-67.2 V in, 91% efficient, USD 88.66) can.

6. Cameras:
- OAK-D Pro W: widest field of view (stereo 127 x 79.5 deg), with IR, 91 g, USD 529.
- RealSense D435i (75 g, 3.4 W, USD 399, out of stock) and D455 (116 g, USD 499).
- OAK-D Lite: now USD 269.

7. Ranging:
- STL-19P (45 g, 1.45 W, USD 96) and RPLIDAR C1 (110 g, USD 80) are the light 2D options.
- Unitree L2 (230 g, 360 x 96 deg, 10-13 W, USD 419) and Livox Mid-360 (265 g, 6.5 W, about USD 999 and being discontinued) cover 3D.
- Pololu ToF boards cost USD 20-25 and weigh about 0.5 g.

8. Safety and tether:
- The FORT wireless e-stop is designed to PLd Cat 3 but is quote-only and needs a separate receiver whose specs I could not get.
- TE LEV100 contactor: 100 A continuous, 190 g, 12/24/48 V coils.
- Bench supplies: the Mean Well RSP-750 (current limit recovers by itself, remote on/off, USD 206) suits motor surges better than the LRS-600 (USD 67), which shuts off after 3 s of overload. Neither can absorb current fed back from the motors.

9. CAN and voice: the PCAN-USB FD (isolated, 12 Mbit/s data, 68 g, USD 368) is the reliable CAN FD option on Jetson. The USD 35 CANable 2.0 only supports CAN FD through beta firmware. ReSpeaker XVF3800: USD 60.99.

Prices are higher in 2026 for Jetson, OAK and RealSense parts, and RealSense adds a tariff surcharge.
